newsitem.title: INDIA: India bank credit disbursals on the increase - SBI.
newsitem.headline: India bank credit disbursals on the increase - SBI.

text.p: The poor credit offtake in the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) year has been reversed in recent months, the State Bank of India (SBI) chairman said on Thursday.
India's largest commercial bank, SBI, reported a 4.13 percent decline in its advances from March 31, 1996 to 496.72 billion rupees as of September 30.
"But decline in bank credit is being reversed. In October and November, we (SBI) saw an increase in bank credit of 17 billion rupees," chairman P.G. Kakodkar said.
Addressing a press conference after releasing the bank's results for the six months ended September 30, 1996, Kakodkar said talk of the country sliding into a recession was premature.
"It is not so...there is no recession," he said.
"A temporary inability on the part of corporates to access the capital market has led to poor demand for credit this year," he said.
Kakodkar said companies which had tied up project finance arrangements were badly stuck for funds when they had to bring in their own stake to the project.
"Borrowers have to put in their own stake before loans are disbursed...It is here that the problem lies. Since the capital market is not doing well this year, companies are unable to raise funds."
This, in turn, led to loans not being drawn upon, he said.
